title_original: Mapping Memory: Moshekwa Langa’s Three Decades of Artistic Exploration

blocks.text: At Kunstinstituut Melly in Rotterdam, South African artist Moshekwa Langa’s ‘You Will Find Us in the Best Places’ brings together nearly 120 works that explore memory, identity, and the shifting relationships between time and place.

How do we map a life shaped by movement, memory and imagination? In ‘You Will Find Us in the Best Places’, South African artist Moshekwa Langa reflects on three decades of artistic practice through his most comprehensive exhibition in the Netherlands to date.

The exhibition occupies all four floors of Kunstinstituut Melly and presents works created between 1995 and 2026. Working across drawing, collage, photography, video and installation, Langa transforms everyday materials, collected objects and fragments of personal experience into layered compositions that blur the boundaries between reality and imagination.
Emerging during South Africa’s transition from apartheid, Langa developed an internationally recognised practice that resists fixed narratives of identity and belonging.

Curated by Gabi Ngcobo and Kabelo Malatsie, the exhibition approaches his work through recurring ideas rather than strict chronology, revealing how memories, places and unfinished narratives continually resurface. From his early participation in international biennials to his ongoing explorations of material and memory, Langa’s practice offers alternative ways of understanding time and experience.
‘You Will Find Us in the Best Places’ invites audiences to encounter an artistic world where histories overlap, beginnings remain open, and meaning is continually reconstructed.
This exhibition will be on view at Kunstinstituut Melly in Rotterdam from 24 October 2026 until 28 March 2027.
